name: Bermondsey Beer Tasting Tour
schedule: Various dates, with start times from midday to 6:30pm
meeting_point: Southwark Brewing, 46 Druid St, London SE1 2EZ
summary: A guided walking tour of the best breweries and taprooms on Bermondsey's famous 'beer mile', led by accredited Beer Sommelier and Certified Cicerone Paul Davies, with tutored tastings at 4 tap rooms.
description_md:
London's craft beer scene is among the most exciting anywhere in the world, and no corner of the city tells its story better than Bermondsey's famous 'beer mile' — a run of railway-arch breweries and taprooms threading through the heart of SE1. This tutored beer tasting tour walks you along the mile in expert company, turning a great afternoon out into a proper education in beer. It's a real step up from the usual crawl: accredited Beer Sommelier and Certified Cicerone® Paul Davies leads the way, with tutored tastings at four of the mile's best taprooms.

# What you'll do

Your guide, accredited Beer Sommelier and Certified Cicerone® Paul Davies, hosts a tutored tasting at every stop — so you leave knowing not just which beers you enjoyed, but why. Along the way you'll pick up the sensory evaluation techniques that professional beer judges use to assess a glass, and hear the history and evolution of the styles you're tasting. This is tutored tasting rather than a rushed pub crawl, with time at each stop to smell, sip and talk through what makes each beer tick. Your four tasting stops are drawn from the mile's best-loved railway-arch breweries and taprooms, among them:

**Southwark Brewing.** The tour's meeting point and an established beer-mile favourite, where you'll settle in for your first tutored tasting.

**Anspach and Hobday.** A behind-the-arches taproom visit with a guided tasting of the styles brewed on site.

**Moor Beer.** Another characterful stop for tasting and expert commentary on what's in your glass.

**Bianca Road.** A modern craft brewery and taproom on the mile, with beers to sample and discuss.

**Mash Paddle.** A welcoming taproom stop for more tutored tasting along the route.

**The Kernel.** One of the names credited with sparking London's craft beer boom, and a fitting stop on any beer-mile tour.

# Good to know

- Lasts 2 to 3.5 hours, depending on your time slot
- Runs on various dates, with start times from midday to 6:30pm
- Meet at Southwark Brewing, 46 Druid Street, London SE1 2EZ
- A guided walking tour along the beer mile — perfect for seasoned beer fans and curious newcomers looking to taste with an expert
- Aged 18+
includes: Tutored beer tasting led by an accredited Beer Sommelier & Certified Cicerone®
Visits to 4 taprooms on the Bermondsey beer mile
Sensory evaluation techniques used by beer judges
The history and evolution of the beer styles you taste

name: Bermondsey Cheese Meat & Beer Tour
meeting_point: Southwark Brewery, 46 Druid Street, London SE1 2EZ
summary: A 2.5-hour guided tasting walk through Bermondsey’s beer mile taprooms, pairing quality British cheese and charcuterie with craft beers — small groups capped at around 13.
description_md:
Cheese, charcuterie and craft beer make one of the great pairings, and this guided tasting walk brings all three together along Bermondsey's famous beer mile in London. Strung out beneath the railway arches south of the river, the beer mile is one of the capital's best-loved craft beer destinations — a run of independent breweries and taprooms that has become a weekend pilgrimage for London's beer lovers. This tour turns a wander between them into a proper food-and-drink experience: a relaxed, sociable brewery tour where quality British cheese and cured meats are matched to the beers in your glass. Across the afternoon your guide leads a beer tasting at every stop, explaining how the flavours on the plate play off the styles on the bar. It's an easy, unhurried way to spend a Saturday among the arches, learning a little as you go.

# What you'll do

**Southwark Brewery.** The tour begins here with a welcome drink and a friendly introduction to the day ahead — the neighbourhood, the beer mile and how the tastings work — so everyone settles in before the walking starts.

**Billy Frank's Jerky.** From there it's on to Billy Frank's for cheese and beer tastings, where your guide talks you through how different British cheeses and cured meats pair with different styles of beer, and why some combinations sing while others clash.

**Anspach & Hobday, Bianca Road or Moor Vaults.** The walk finishes in one of these neighbouring beer-mile taprooms for a final tasting, rounding out three venues in all. There's at least one tasting at every stop, with beer, cheese and charcuterie throughout, plus expert food-and-beer pairing guidance from a knowledgeable guide — so you come away with a real feel for what makes a good match work and a few ideas to try at home.

# Good to know

- Approximately 2.5 hours
- Runs on Saturdays, 12pm–2:30pm
- Meet at Southwark Brewery, 46 Druid Street, London SE1 2EZ — a short walk from London Bridge station
- Small groups, capped at around 13 — a sociable choice for friends, couples and anyone who loves good food and beer
- Comfortable shoes are a good idea for the short walk between taprooms
- Aged 18+
- Gift vouchers available

name: The Leeds Heritage Pub Tour
summary: A three-and-a-half-hour exploration of over 300 years of Leeds pub and brewing history, led by local expert guide Mike, with a half pint included at each historic pub stop from The Tetley to Whitelock's Ale House.
description_md:
Enjoy an exploration of over 300 years of pub and brewing history in Leeds, led by local expert and passionate independent tour guide Mike. Fully self-researched, this three-and-a-half-hour tour brings to life stories of the people, places and events that shaped the city's incredible pub heritage, with drinks included to keep everyone refreshed along the way.

# The route

Starting at The Tetley, hear the two-century story of Tetley Brewery, which went on to become one of Yorkshire's most beloved, and Britain's largest. The tour then heads on to the Adelphi, a classic late Victorian pub. Understand how the architecture played an important part of the Victorian pub experience, before watching heritage video artefacts showing what life was like for one of Leeds' breweries in the early and mid-20th century. From here, the group will then head for a walk through Brewery Wharf, stopping at various points of interest on the way. The next stop is the Lamb & Flag, where a fun map reading task will take place, before hearing the history of the building, opened in 1801. Then it's time for another walk, this time to explore some ghost pubs of Leeds – buildings that used to be pubs, with evidence still in the architecture. This leads the group to the White Swan, with a history that ties it closely to neighbouring City Varieties Music Hall. Here, explore a modern map of Leeds City Centre and learn how brewing has evolved in the area. The final tour stop is Whitelock's Ale House, arguably Leeds' jewel in the pub crown. Founded in 1715, the pub boasts a fascinating history which Mike will explain unvarnished to finish the tour.

# Drinks along the way

Throughout the tour, Mike will tell you stories from old local newspapers and books, show and use old maps and images and lots more to bring history to life. At each pub stop, a half pint is included for each guest. Enjoy either hand-pulled ale, draught lager or cider, or a soft drink. For tour timings and guest wellbeing, upgrades to pints or higher alcohol content drinks such as wines and spirits are not offered as part of this tour.

# Your guide

Your guide Mike is Leeds born and bred. He is currently the serving Secretary of the British Guild of Beer Writers and has a background that has seen him operate a micro-brewery, run a pub, organise beer festivals and serve as the Chair for the Leeds branch of the Campaign for Real Ale.

name: Kent Hop Farm Tour at Hukins Hops
schedule: Selected Saturdays during the season, with 11am, 1pm and 3pm time slots
meeting_point: Hukins Hops, Haffenden Farms, Bugglesden Rd, St Michaels, Tenterden TN30 6TG (at the taproom)
summary: A two-hour guided tour of the working Hukins Hops farm in Kent — walk the 18-foot-high hop gardens, see the picking and processing facility in action, then relax in the taproom. Children attend free with a paying adult.
description_md:
Kent has earned its nickname as the Garden of England partly on the back of hops — the county has grown them for the beer world for centuries. This experience takes you deep into that story at Hukins Hops, a working farm near Tenterden, and it's a world away from the usual brewery tour: instead of a brewhouse, you spend your visit out among the towering hop gardens that supply Britain's craft breweries. Whether you're a curious first-timer or a seasoned beer geek, it's a rare chance in Kent to connect the raw ingredient with the finished pint — before settling in for a beer in the farm taproom.

# What you'll do

Your guided visit begins out in the hop gardens themselves, where you'll walk beneath bines trained up to eighteen feet high and learn how different hop varieties are selected and grown to meet the demands of today's fast-moving craft beer market — and how those hops go on to shape the aroma and flavour of the beer you drink. From there you'll head into the modern picking and processing facility to see the machinery in action, discovering how great British engineering and modern technology combine to pick, dry and process hundreds of thousands of hop plants during the short, intense weeks of harvest.

Throughout, your guide shares the story of Kent's long hop-growing heritage and explains what it means for the county's brewing today, from the fields around you to the pint in your hand. Once the tour wraps up, there's time to unwind in the on-site taproom at your own pace, with beer and food available to buy so you can raise a glass to the harvest before you head home.

# Good to know

- Tours last approximately 2 hours, with 11am, 1pm and 3pm slots on selected Saturdays during the season
- Meet at the taproom: Hukins Hops, Haffenden Farms, Bugglesden Rd, St Michaels, Tenterden TN30 6TG
- A great fit for hop lovers and beer enthusiasts alike, whether you're an amateur or an experienced drinker
- Children are welcome and attend free with a paying adult
- Groups are capped at around 20 people
- Tickets are non-refundable and non-exchangeable after purchase

The tour begins within the walls of Cardiff's iconic city-centre castle, where your group gathers just inside the South Gate for a meet-up and a relaxed introduction to the tour ahead. You'll get a real sense of the people and craft behind each beer, not just the finished pint.

Across three different Cardiff brewery taprooms you'll enjoy beers at every stop, moving between specialist craft beer bars and taprooms at an easy, sociable pace. Your guide is on hand throughout to talk you through each carefully selected pour, explaining how the ingredients and brewing methods combine to create the flavours you're tasting. The focus stays firmly on quality, independent beer from local Welsh suppliers, so you'll finish the tour knowing a good deal more about what makes Cardiff's brewing scene worth seeking out. It's an easygoing, hands-on introduction to why Welsh brewing is having such a moment.

# Good to know

- A private group experience for a minimum of 10 people — ideal for celebrations, get-togethers and corporate days out
- Includes a guided tour, a behind-the-scenes brewery visit and beer tastings at each stop
- Starts inside Cardiff Castle, just within the South Gate entrance on Castle Street (CF10 3RB)

name: Heist Brewery Tours
summary: A weekly one-hour tour of Heist Brew Co in Sheffield, seeing the brewing process behind the beers and enjoying 3 x 1/3 pints of Heist beers fresh from the tap.
description_md:
Sheffield has long been regarded as one of Britain's great beer cities, with a dense concentration of breweries and taprooms packed into its old industrial quarters — and few names capture that independent swagger better than Heist Brew Co. This weekly brewery tour and beer tasting takes you inside one of the city's most exciting breweries, following the journey from raw ingredients to finished pint before you settle in to sample the results straight from the tap. It's a relaxed hour that suits curious first-timers and committed craft beer fans alike.

# What you'll do

Heist Brew Co began brewing in Clowne, Derbyshire back in 2018 and swiftly earned a reputation for bold, modern beers across a huge range of styles. The team has since moved to Sheffield, expanding their fermentation capacity and opening a brilliant taproom, and they now brew flat out to keep the taps flowing. Once a week they throw open the doors to show you exactly how it's all done, and there's no better place to get properly acquainted with the beers.

Your guide walks you through the brewing process, from the raw ingredients that go into the mash to the finished beer resting in the tanks — a proper behind-the-scenes look at a working brewery in full flow. When the tour wraps up, you'll take a seat in the taproom for three fresh thirds of Heist beer, poured straight from the tap so you're tasting it at its very best. The third-pint measures let you compare a spread of styles rather than committing to a single pint, which makes this a great way to get to know a brewery you might only have met on a shop shelf.

# Good to know

- Runs every Friday, 4pm–5pm — around one hour in total
- Includes 3 x 1/3 pints of Heist beers, poured fresh from the tap
- A behind-the-scenes look at the brewing process at a working Sheffield brewery
- Great for curious first-timers and committed craft beer fans alike
- Contact us for current pricing and availability

Moorhouse's is one of Burnley's most celebrated breweries and a long-standing part of Lancashire's brewing heritage. This behind-the-scenes brewery tour is a warm, welcoming way to get to know it: you'll go behind the scenes to see how the beer is made, then settle in for a proper Lancashire pie and pea supper. It's a relaxed session built around good beer and good food, arranged by prior appointment in Burnley.

# What you'll do

Your visit centres on Moorhouse's Brewery, one of the enduring names in Lancashire beer. A 45-minute guided tour leads you behind the scenes to see how the beers are made and hear the story behind one of Burnley's best-known independent producers, from the raw ingredients through to the finished pint. It's an unhurried, informative look at a working brewery, led by people who know it inside out, and you'll come away with a real sense of the craft and local character behind every batch.

name: Hackney Wick Craft Beer Experience
meeting_point: The White Building, Unit 7 Queens Yard, London E9 5EN (outside Crate Brewery car park)
summary: A 2-hour guided tour of Hackney Wick’s canal-side microbreweries and craft beer bars, led by a local beer expert and professional brewer — five beer tastings across three venues, plus a shareable cheese platter.
description_md:
Tucked into the canal-side warehouses of east London, Hackney Wick has grown into one of the capital's most exciting craft beer neighbourhoods — a tight cluster of microbreweries and taprooms all within easy strolling distance of one another. This Hackney Wick brewery tour and beer tasting is led by a local beer expert and professional brewer, giving you an insider's route through the area over a relaxed Saturday afternoon in London. It's a genuine taste of the city's independent brewing scene, poured fresh at source. London's craft beer boom has spread far beyond the city centre, and Hackney Wick sits right at its creative edge, where breweries share the same cobbled yards as artists' studios and waterside cafés.

# What you'll do

Over roughly two hours you'll visit three venues — two working breweries and a craft beer bar — sampling five different beers along the way. They're served in 1/3 and 1/2 pint measures, so you can explore a wider range of styles at a comfortable pace while your guide talks you through what's in each glass and how it was made. Starting outside Crate Brewery, you'll follow a gentle walking route of around a mile that links Hackney Wick's canal-side breweries and taprooms.

A shareable cheese platter is included as you go, with a vegan alternative available. Because your guide is a working brewer, you'll get a real behind-the-scenes perspective on everything you taste — the ingredients, the brewing process and the stories behind these independent east London producers. Expect a friendly, unhurried afternoon rather than a rush between stops, with plenty of chance to ask questions and pick up recommendations for the neighbourhood.

# Good to know

- Runs on selected Saturdays, 12:30pm–2:30pm — around two hours in total
- Meet outside Crate Brewery's car park at The White Building, Unit 7 Queens Yard, London E9 5EN — nearest station Hackney Wick
- Five beers plus a shareable cheese platter, with a vegan option available
- Around a mile of walking; all venues and toilets are step-free and wheelchair accessible
- Ideal for beer lovers, friends and small celebrations keen to discover east London's independent brewing scene
- Groups of up to 25
- Aged 18+
